description: Biophysical reaction-diffusion and evolutionary game engine resolving the post-ADAURA osimertinib cessation dilemma via cylindrical Bessel transport.
name: spatial-continuum

metadata.abstract:
Background: In early-stage EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), 36 months of adjuvant osimertinib significantly prolongs disease-free survival (ADAURA trial). However, longitudinal minimal residual disease tracking reveals an alarming post-cessation phenomenon: among patients who experience disease recurrence, 67.9% of all recurrence events occur after the planned 36-month discontinuation, with 57.9% clustering within the first 12 months post-cessation. Current clinical oncology operates without a mechanistic rationale to distinguish patients who are cured from those who harbor occult micrometastases held in cytostatic dormancy. Furthermore, conventional drug discovery relies on the "pharmacological fallacy" that resistance is solely a pocket-level biochemical phenomenon to be addressed by successive drug generations, ignoring the spatial microenvironmental architecture of mass transport.

Methods:

We established a multi-scale biophysical reaction-diffusion framework coupling Starling-Darcy fluid mechanics, Stokes-Einstein tissue transport, and modified cylindrical Bessel functions of the second kind (K0) to define the spatial limits of pharmacological penetration across tumor cords. The model was parameterized using human clinical pharmacokinetic measurements and human lung cancer interstitial fluid pressure (IFP) manometry in freshly resected specimens (N = 211, Mori et al. 2015). The framework was validated across 6 independent cohorts totaling 3,205 human patients, including the ADAURA ctDNA cohort (N = 220), MSKCC thoracic surgical histology (N = 604), multi-center transcriptomic validation (N = 854), MSKCC targeted genomic co-alteration (N = 863), and the Phase III RELAY trial (N = 449). The model was subjected to an adversarial stress-testing suite evaluating biophysical singularities, Peclet number breakdown, pharmacokinetic perturbations, and ctDNA false-negative blind spots.

Results:

In solid tumor cords, interstitial fluid pressure extinguishes convective transvascular flow (Peclet Pe < 0.1), establishing diffusion dominance. Free osimertinib decays beneath the therapeutic IC50 threshold at a critical radius rcrit ≈ 166 μm. In cords where intercapillary half-distance exceeds rcrit, viable oxygenated tumor cells (rox = 200 μm) inhabit a mandatory pharmacological sanctuary of width Δr = 34.1 μm (31.3% of cord volume), where chronic sub-inhibitory exposure enforces cytostatic G0/G1 dormancy. Analytical tumor repopulation kinetics predicted a median clinical ctDNA-to-CT lead time of 5.37 months, matching human clinical confidence intervals in ADAURA (95% CI: 2.2-5.6 months). Integrating spatial histology (S), co-genomics (G), and ctDNA kinetics (M), we formulated the Bedside Composite Resistance Index (CRI = 0.40S + 0.35G + 0.25M) and designed the prospective Phase III SG-ADAURA trial (N = 800) evaluating CRI-guided treatment extension and anti-VEGFR2 vascular normalization.

Conclusions:

Post-adjuvant osimertinib relapse is primarily driven by physical tissue-level sanctuaries rather than immediate catalytic site mutations. The CRI engine transitions oncology from empirical trial-and-error to biophysically grounded precision decision-making.
metadata.title: The Spatial-Genomic Oncology Continuum: A Biophysical Reaction-Diffusion Theory of Pharmacological Sanctuaries, the Post-ADAURA Cessation Dilemma, and the SG-ADAURA Clinical Trial Protocol
